candidate_relations.reason: The echocardiogram confirmed dilated cardiomyopathy with EF 30-35%, making this a documented finding/complication. However, the benchmark diagnosis is Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C), which is the unifying syndrome explaining the cardiac, renal, gastrointestinal, neurological, and inflammatory features together. Dilated cardiomyopathy is a component manifestation, not the final diagnostic entity.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Dilated cardiomyopathy with reduced EF is a cardiac manifestation documented in this case but is not the overarching diagnosis; MIS-C encompasses multi-organ involvement including but not limited to the cardiac findings

case_quality_flags: Patient is 18 years old, at the upper age boundary for MIS-C (typically <21 years per CDC criteria); MIS-A (adults) is an alternative framing but reference diagnosis is MIS-C
SARS-CoV-2 PCR negative; serology not reported, which is relevant to MIS-C criteria requiring evidence of prior COVID-19 exposure
Positive beta2-glycoprotein IgA antiphospholipid antibody raises antiphospholipid syndrome as a competing diagnosis, though low complement and multisystem inflammation favor MIS-C
